question: Your team must replace an in-house HTTP client library with a new library across about 50 files in the repository. Two integration approaches are possible, and each approach needs different infrastructure. A teammate wants Claude Code to start editing files right away. Which way of working with Claude Code fits this task best?

options.text: Use direct execution for each file, because each single edit is a small, well-scoped change to one function.
options.reason: The task as a whole has architectural implications and two valid integration approaches, so it needs plan mode; direct execution fits only changes whose overall scope is simple and clear.

options.text: Start in plan mode so that Claude Code explores the codebase and designs the migration approach before any file is changed.
options.reason: Plan mode is designed for large-scale, multi-file changes with multiple valid approaches and architectural decisions, and it allows safe exploration and design before changes are committed, which prevents costly rework.

options.text: Give the whole migration to the Explore subagent so that its verbose output stays out of the main conversation context.
options.reason: The Explore subagent isolates verbose discovery output and returns summaries to preserve context; it does not replace plan mode for deciding the architecture of a large migration.

options.text: Use direct execution and let Claude Code edit the files one after another, fixing problems as they appear during the migration.
options.reason: Direct execution is for simple, well-scoped changes; using it for a migration across many files with an open choice of approach risks costly rework.
